consequence: The claim that the model 'can detect when the chain is broken' is refuted, not merely unsupported, and must be removed from the paper.
interpretation: Supplying a broken chain makes the model LESS likely to answer Unknown, not more: 42.2% against a 75.0% baseline, -32.8pp. A validity tracker would move the other way. The model emits `No` on 110/192 under broken_chain and on exactly 110/192 under truncate_1 as well; what separates the two arms is Yes (1 vs 61), i.e. whether a final inference is completable. So the model is not detecting invalidity — it completes when it can and falls back when it cannot, and the fallback itself shifts once any query-relevant certificate is present.
